title: Angles from Intersecting Chords Practice
description: Practice using intercepted arcs to find angles formed by chords intersecting inside circles.

questions.question: Two chords intersect inside a circle. The intercepted arcs for an angle measure 80 degrees and 120 degrees. What is the angle measure?
For two chords intersecting inside a circle, the angle measure equals half the sum of the measures of its intercepted arcs.
questions.explanation: Interior angles formed by intersecting chords use m angle = 1/2(arc 1 + arc 2).

questions.question: An interior chord angle intercepts arcs of 50 degrees and 90 degrees. What is the angle measure?
Two intercepted arcs measure 35 degrees and 105 degrees. Enter the interior angle measure in degrees.
An interior angle measures 65 degrees. One intercepted arc measures 40 degrees. What is the other intercepted arc?
questions.explanation: Double the angle first: 2(65) = 130. Then 130 - 40 = 90 degrees.

questions.question: If an interior chord angle measures 90 degrees, then the two intercepted arcs used for that angle have a sum of 180 degrees.
questions.explanation: The angle is half the arc sum, so the arc sum is twice the angle: 2(90) = 180 degrees.

questions.question: An interior chord angle measures 58 degrees. One intercepted arc is 46 degrees. Enter the other intercepted arc in degrees.
questions.explanation: The arc sum is 2(58) = 116 degrees. The missing arc is 116 - 46 = 70 degrees.

questions.question: Explain why an angle formed by two chords inside a circle with intercepted arcs 100 degrees and 60 degrees measures 80 degrees.
questions.correctAnswer: For intersecting chords inside a circle, the angle is half the sum of the intercepted arcs. Since 100 + 60 = 160 and half of 160 is 80, the angle is 80 degrees.
questions.explanation: A complete response should name the half-sum rule and show the arithmetic.
